title: The higher-outerplanarity obstruction conjecture for completely independent spanning trees
statement:
A **triangulated disc** is a plane graph whose bounded faces are triangles, and a graph is **$k$-outerplanar** if it has a planar embedding whose vertices become empty after repeatedly removing the vertices on the outer face $k$ times. A **completely independent spanning tree** (CIST) is a spanning tree with the pairwise independence property described in the paper.

**Higher-outerplanarity obstruction conjecture.** For any $k\geq 4$, there exists a 3-connected $k$-outerplanar triangulated disc with no completely independent spanning trees.

The paper constructs such an example for $k=4$, showing the first case of the proposed obstruction; the assertion for all $k\geq4$ remains open in the supplied text.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12827

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2026). “However, P\'{e}terfalvi disproved this conjecture by constructing a $k$-connected graph that does not have two CISTs for any $k \geq 2$.”
source_name: Toru Araki, “Completely Independent Spanning Trees in k-Outerplanar Triangulated Discs”, arXiv:2606.12827 (2026).
